question: The chart below shows the number of men and women in further education in Britain in three periods and whether they were studying full-time or part-time.
essay:
The bar chart illustrates the number of male and female students in full-time and part-time education in Britain across three periods: 1970/71, 1980/81, and 1990/91. Overall, part-time education was significantly more popular than full-time education for both genders throughout the entire period.

In terms of part-time education, approximately 1,000 thousand males were in education in 1970/71. This figure fluctuated slightly, dropping to roughly 850 thousand in 1980/81 before rising again to around 900 thousand by 1990/91. By contrast, the number of female part-time students began at only around 700 thousand in 1970/71, but grew substantially over the two decades, exceeding 1,100 thousand in 1990/91 and surpassing male numbers.
